title: Ruby on Rails Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Make a controller action
examples.description: A route names a controller and action. GET /hello runs LessonController#hello.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/hello", to: "lesson#hello"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def hello
 render plain: "Hello, Asha!"
end
end

examples.title: Render JSON data
examples.description: render json turns a Ruby value into a JSON response. Open GET /book.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/book", to: "lesson#book"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def book
 render json: { title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24 }
end
end

examples.title: Read a path input
examples.description: A colon marks a route value. GET /hello/Ravi places Ravi in params[:name].
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/hello/:name", to: "lesson#hello"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def hello
 render plain: "Hi, #{params[:name]}!"
end
end

examples.title: Read query data
examples.description: params also contains query values. Open GET /search?q=cat.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/search", to: "lesson#search"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def search
 render json: { term: params[:q] || "" }
end
end

examples.title: Read a JSON request
examples.description: Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. Rails puts body values in params.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
post "/books", to: "lesson#create"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def create
 if !params[:title].is_a?(String)
  render json: { error: "Title needed" }, status: :bad_request
  return
 end
 render json: { title: params[:title] }, status: :created
end
end

examples.title: Choose allowed inputs
examples.description: permit chooses allowed parameter keys. Send POST /books with title and an extra secret key; only title is returned.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
post "/books", to: "lesson#create"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def create
 allowed = params.permit(:title)
 render json: allowed
end
end

examples.title: Report a missing item
examples.description: Rails status symbols name HTTP statuses. Open GET /missing.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/missing", to: "lesson#missing"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def missing
 render json: { error: "Book not found" }, status: :not_found
end
end

examples.title: Build a path from a route helper
examples.description: The as option names a route helper. Open GET /link to see the helper fill in a name.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/hello/:name", to: "lesson#hello", as: :hello
get "/link", to: "lesson#link"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def hello
 render plain: params[:name]
end
def link
 render plain: hello_path(name: "Asha")
end
end

examples.title: Redirect a client
examples.description: redirect_to sends a Location header. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/start", to: "lesson#start"
get "/hello", to: "lesson#hello"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def start
 redirect_to "/hello"
end
def hello
 render plain: "Welcome"
end
end

examples.title: Set response metadata
examples.description: response.headers holds reply headers. Open GET /note.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/note", to: "lesson#note"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def note
 response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
 render plain: "Practice note"
end
end

examples.title: Run a shared step
examples.description: before_action runs before controller actions. GET /school reads the value set by the callback.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
get "/school", to: "lesson#school"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
before_action :set_school
def school
 render plain: @school
end
private
def set_school
 @school = "Oak School"
end
end

examples.title: Return an empty successful reply
examples.description: head sends a status and no body. DELETE /books/1 returns 204 in this practice-only action.
examples.code:
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
delete "/books/:id", to: "lesson#destroy"
end

# app/controllers/lesson_controller.rb
class LessonController < ActionController::API
def destroy
 head :no_content
end
end
